subject: research/marine-detect
professional: a maritime-perception researcher who reviews USV obstacle-detection papers (MODS/LaRS-style benchmark work). The first things they check are the evaluation protocol (what counts as an obstacle, minimum size, connectivity, how it compares to MODS), whether a baseline from the literature is reproduced, and whether the degradation model is physically grounded

evidence.correctness: MaSTr1325 is unreachable from this session (data.vicos.si: proxy connect_rejected 403), so training and inference were not rerun; correctness rests on recomputing every headline from the committed per-object records in experiments/runs/*.json with an independent script (scratchpad/marine-detect/recompute.py, scipy t-quantiles, imports nothing from marine_detect). All README/results.txt numbers reproduce exactly: lraspp-clean recall 0.319 +- 0.049, >=16 px 0.602 +- 0.122, fog t=0.3 0.280, t=0.15 0.226, aug 0.645 and 0.613, false alarms 0.078 -> 0.283 (3.63x, README 3.6x); Koschmieder d/V for t=0.5/0.3/0.15 = 0.177/0.308/0.485 (README 18/31/48%); t(0.975, df=2)=4.3027, df=1=12.706 match the T95 table; 16 px x (512/320)(384/240) = 40.96 (README 41 px); binomial half-width at p=0.6, n=31 = 0.172 (README +-17). The scored quantity itself is inflated: scipy ndimage.label is called with its default 4-connectivity (metrics.py:35), so a diagonal 8-pixel line becomes 8 one-pixel 'floating obstacles' (auditor's synthetic check). In the committed records 80 of the 204 test 'floating obstacles' are single pixels and 117 are 3 px or less; frame 73 alone contributes 7 components on consecutive rows 178-185. The headline '32% of 204' therefore counts annotation fragments as obstacles. Reading the arithmetic plus not rerunning the model caps this at 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: block split (test passes, 1025/300 recorded in every run file), LR-ASPP and pixel-MLP runs for 3 seeds each (9 JSON files present), fog and glint sweeps (8 conditions in every file), recall by size and by rows below the water edge (results.txt, horizon_rows.json present), figure (fig_degradation.png present), live page (research/_homepage/build.py builds research/marine-detect/index.html, 22,967 bytes, with the 'not a certified perception system' line). Next steps (MODS, WaSR, depth fog, colregs link) are correctly labelled not done. The README's SHA-256 promise is half done: hashes are in data.py but no code verifies them. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: PYTHONPATH=src /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest tests -q: 10 passed in 0.59 s. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 1 of 6 caught (removing the frame-touch check). Survived: found threshold >= -> >, false-alarm size floor 4 -> >8, removing the mostly-water ring filter entirely, fog airlight term (1-t) -> (1-t)^2 (the test only pins t=1 and t~0), and the n=3 t-quantile 4.303 -> 2.0 (aggregate.py has no tests at all). The training/predict path (model.py) has no test.
evidence.craft: Read data.py, degrade.py, metrics.py, model.py, run.py, aggregate.py, horizon.py, tests. Small, readable, well-commented modules. Defects: default 4-connectivity in both component labellings (metrics.py:35, :69) with no stated choice; SHA256 dict in data.py:22 is never checked; obstacle_recall/binned_recall and AREA_BINS (0,64,256,1024) in metrics.py give recall_by_area bins that differ from the bins aggregate.py reports (0,8,16,32,64,256), so the JSON's recall_by_area field is unused; false-alarm rule excludes any blob that touches an unknown pixel (on_water == size), undocumented. No dead engines or copied code.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: every table number in README and project.json lede matches results.txt and the run JSONs (pass); disclaimer 'Research code, not a certified perception system' on README and built page (pass); data licence and citations (pass). Not backed or overstated: (1) README:24 calls the 173 sub-16-px components 'distant buoys and swimmers, and fragments' while 80 of 204 are single pixels, largely 4-connectivity fragments; (2) README:28 'falls from 60% to 28%' at t=0.3 has a 95% interval of +-28 points (results.txt), shown without it; (3) README:41-42 'a rerun of one seed moved clean mIoU by 0.002' has no file (not in LOG.md or runs/); (4) README:60 'SHA-256 of the two archives used here' are listed but never verified by code.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it: per-object records (frame, area, found, coverage, waterline row) are committed, so any rebinning is possible without retraining, and the reproduce block is complete. Nearest prior work: WaSR (Bovcon and Kristan 2022) and MODS are cited and honestly not reproduced; eWaSR (Tersek, Zust and Kristan 2023, an embedded-compute lightweight WaSR on MaSTr1325/MODS) is the closest prior lightweight-network result and is not cited; LaRS includes adverse-condition scenes. Novelty is modest: fog/glint degradation curves for a MobileNetV3 LR-ASPP on MaSTr1325 with a mask-derived detection score. Sound as a preliminary baseline, but the detection number is not comparable to MODS and is dominated by 1-px components, so it cannot yet feed marine-colregs as a miss-rate model.
evidence.domain: Against MODS practice (box-annotated obstacles, detection via coverage, minimum-size handling) the mask analogue departs in three ways a reviewer would hit first: 4-connected components fragment thin diagonal structures; there is no minimum object size for ground truth while predicted blobs under 4 px can never be false alarms (an asymmetric rule); masks are NEAREST-downsampled 1.6x before labelling, which further breaks thin objects. The Koschmieder model and the d/V conversion are textbook-correct; uniform transmission is acknowledged as a limitation. Glint is stylised and declared as such.

defects.what: Floating obstacles are labelled with scipy's default 4-connectivity, so thin diagonal structures split into many 1-px 'obstacles' (synthetic diagonal 8-px line -> 8 obstacles). 80 of the 204 test obstacles are single pixels and 117 are <= 3 px; the headline '32% of 204 floating obstacles found' and 'misses most floating obstacles' rest on this count

README describes the sub-16-px set as 'distant buoys and swimmers, and fragments of thin structures' and leads with recall over all 204, while the set is dominated by single-pixel components; the lede and research index repeat '32% of 204'

Asymmetric size rule: ground-truth obstacles count from 1 px, predicted blobs under 4 px are never false alarms, and any blob touching an unknown pixel is excluded; not MODS practice and not stated as a departure

Tests miss core metric and degradation logic: 5 of 6 seeded mutants survive (found threshold, FA size floor, water-ring filter removed, fog airlight term, t-quantile); experiments/aggregate.py and model.py are untested
'falls from 60% to 28%' at t=0.3 is reported without its 95% interval of +-28 points (results.txt), which spans 0 to 56%
'a rerun of one seed moved clean mIoU by 0.002' is backed by no file
Archive SHA-256 constants are defined but never verified; README implies they pin the data used
Nearest lightweight prior work, eWaSR (Tersek, Zust and Kristan 2023, Sensors), is not cited or compared

verdict: A tidy, honest preliminary baseline whose reported arithmetic is exactly right and whose headline detection number counts annotation fragments as obstacles. Every table value (recall 0.319 +- 0.049, >=16 px 0.602, fog 0.280/0.226, glint false alarms 0.078 -> 0.283) reproduces from the committed per-object records with an independent scipy script, and the Koschmieder d/V fractions and t-quantiles are textbook-correct. But metrics.py labels components with 4-connectivity and no minimum size, so a diagonal 8-px line becomes eight 1-px obstacles; 80 of the 204 test 'floating obstacles' are single pixels, which drives the lead claim that the network 'misses most floating obstacles'. The false-alarm rule is asymmetric to it (blobs under 4 px never count), 5 of 6 seeded mutants survive the 10 tests, and the model could not be rerun here (MaSTr1325 host blocked). Novelty over WaSR/eWaSR/MODS is modest and eWaSR is uncited. Does not meet the bar (verification 1, correctness 2, claims 2); finished for what it claims (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: 8-connectivity plus a stated minimum object size (needs the dataset to re-score; the committed records cannot be re-labelled), hedge the README lead meanwhile, and pin metric thresholds and fog midpoints in tests.
